title: Bounded run of the canonicality guard
statement: Let $F$ be a machine format, and let $\alpha$, $bits$, and $rest$ be Boolean words such that parsing $\alpha$ as a paired encoding returns $(bits,rest)$. Set $B=\max\{F.\mathrm{guard},(4F.\mathrm{k}+5)3^{F.\mathrm{k}+1}\}$ and $j=2|bits|+2$. There exist a position bound $j\le|\alpha|$ and a time $T\le(B+4)(|\alpha|+1)+2(|bits|+1)$ such that the binary guard machine with block parameter $B-1$, started at position $j$ with empty output and counter tape containing the fixed-width increment of $bits$ followed by a zero, is in its done state at time $T$ if $B(\operatorname{value}(bits)+1)\le|rest|$, and in its escape state otherwise; its output is empty, and its input-head position is respectively $j+B(\operatorname{value}(bits)+1)+1$ or $|\alpha|+1$. Neither terminal state occurs at any time strictly before $T$.
